Metrie announces organizational changes across Western Canada distribution network
November 19, 2026 | 8:10 am CST
Metrie announces organizational changes across Western Canada distribution network
In Calgary, Metrie is expanding its existing distribution center by approximately 50,000 square feet.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia — Metrie, #16 on the FDMC 300 list, announced a coordinated series of investments and operational changes across its Western Canada distribution network to strengthen customer service, expand exterior door production capabilities and create a more efficient platform for long-term growth.
The changes include an expanded Calgary, Alberta facility, the transition of Edmonton distribution activities into Calgary, the planned move from Metrie’s Langley, B.C. distribution centre to a more modern facility in nearby Pitt Meadows, B.C., and the renewal of the company’s Winnipeg, Manitoba lease for five years.

“By taking a connected, long-term view of our Western Canada network, we are strengthening the capabilities and capacity needed to serve customers as their needs evolve,” commented Ashik Bhat, vice president, Canada Pro, Metrie. “These investments will help us deliver a broader range of millwork solutions, improve service across the region and create a stronger platform for sustainable growth.”

In Calgary, Metrie is expanding its existing distribution center by approximately 50,000 square feet. The larger footprint will support additional interior and exterior door production capabilities, including door equipment acquired from Owens Corning’s Doors Business, and is expected to allow for expanded services such as painting, pre-finishing, staining and special-order assembly.

In British Columbia, Metrie is concluding the sale of its existing Langley property and the lease of a new 120,000-square-foot facility in nearby Pitt Meadows. The new location will enable improvements in product and operational flow, warehouse-management capabilities, and provide additional door production capacity for the region, including markets such as multifamily and high-rise construction.

As part of the network changes, Metrie will consolidate its Edmonton distribution activities into its Calgary facility and close the Edmonton branch by the end of the year. The company will continue working with affected associates to review available opportunities and provide support through the transition.

“These changes are designed to make the Western Canada network simpler, more capable and more efficient,” commented Peter Kozak, senior director, Transformation and Operations, Canada. “With expanded space in Calgary, upgraded capability in British Columbia and a renewed commitment in Winnipeg, we will be better positioned to build and move product, serve customers and support the next phase of growth.”

Together, the changes are expected to enhance product availability, strengthen interior and exterior door services, and create a more responsive distribution network for customers across Western Canada. Similar modernization initiatives are under way in Eastern Canada. They also support Metrie’s continued investment in the people, facilities and capabilities required to meet changing market needs and pursue long-term growth.
